A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UGround work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–G are readable and support comparison, including matching figures across renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original UGround segmentation results, component ablations, computational measurements and qualitative predictions in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds comparative qualitative predictions in Figure 4.

M1.justification: Policy-Prompted Masking, stochastic layer selection, similarity-map prompting, rewards and training losses remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and Equations 4–9 specify the same procedure; the rewritten Appendix C.3 example introduces no method component.

E1.justification: ReasonSeg, RefCOCO(+/g), gRefCOCO, MUSE, FP-RefCOCO(+/g) and the documented training-data families are retained. New and revised qualitative examples remain within existing reasoning and generalized referring segmentation coverage.

E2.justification: New Figure 4 compares ReasonSeg predictions against LISA, SESAME, READ, GSVA, PixelLM and GLaMM. This includes GLaMM in a ReasonSeg comparison, whereas v2 compared it quantitatively on RefCOCO(+/g). Comparator membership in the quantitative tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Quantitative splits, preprocessing, metrics and training settings are unchanged. Qualitative evaluation inputs change: v4 introduces a six-case ReasonSeg comparison, revises the requested objects in the bench/dog and teddy-bear examples, and replaces a people/motorbike example with bowls. These changes do not establish quantitative reruns.

E4.justification: Figure 4 and Section 5.4 add comparative case analysis of foreground localization, small parts and erroneous masks. Appendix instance-segmentation cases are also revised. Existing component ablations, soft-gating comparison and layer-activation analyses remain intact.

E5.justification: Neither version changes experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance testing. The Monte Carlo interpretation of stochastic layer selection already appears in v2; its rewritten example adds no empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Quantitative table values are unchanged, including UGround-13B's ReasonSeg test scores of 65.0 gIoU and 65.5 cIoU. v4 adds comparative mask predictions and replaces several appendix predictions. Because some prompts also change, the revised masks do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, policy-gradient formulation, Gaussian mask construction and objectives are retained. Appendix C.3 clarifies the ordering of an existing illustrative sequence of forward passes without changing mathematical reasoning or adding a proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about attribute-based unification, dynamic intermediate-layer selection and mask prompting. Their scientific scope and headline performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 5.4 interprets comparative masks as evidence of stronger functional/commonsense grounding and fine-grained part localization, with cleaner boundaries than competing methods. The existing mechanism discussion and Appendix G limitations concerning geometric alignment and mask failures remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 newly identifies Fudan University's CFFF platform as the computational infrastructure used. GPU specifications, training durations, hyperparameters, preprocessing, repository information and code/model availability remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds AnchorSeg (Qian et al., 2026) to the introduction and bibliography without evaluating it as a baseline. The related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain stable. Consolidating duplicate SEEM references and correcting bibliographic metadata do not introduce another research-positioning change.

P1.justification: v4 adds Section 5.4 and acknowledgments, lightly rewrites Appendix C.3, and edits punctuation, affiliations and publication text. Most paragraphs, section organization and the overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figure 4, enlarges ablation Tables 6–8, and revises several appendix image panels and captions. Existing figures are renumbered, one retained heatmap figure is downsampled, and the conclusion and references reflow. Most displays and the overall layout remain stable.

improvement.justification: Figure 4 and Section 5.4 provide direct comparisons of mask quality that v2 lacked. Revised appendix queries illustrate separate object instances more clearly, and larger ablation tables improve readability. These limited gains outweigh the reduced zoom detail of one retained heatmap. The method, quantitative evidence and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
